text.p: France coach Aime Jacquet is continuing his quest for the right World Cup attacking formation with a new call to Christophe Dugarry, the AC Milan striker injured during the European championship finals in June.
Jacquet included Dugarry, who injured his knee during the Euro 96 quarter-final against the Netherlands, when he named his 18-man squad on Tuesday for the friendly away to Portugal next week.

At the back, defender Patrick Blondeau, who will be 29 five days after the January 22 match in Braga, earned his first international call late in his career in recognition of his contribution to French first division leaders Monaco's title challenge.

Bordeaux's France under-21 midfielder Ibrahima Ba, who has been courted by Barcelona, was also picked along with four Italy-based midfielders including the well established Juventus pair Didier Deschamps, France's captain, and Zinedine Zidane.
Jacquet looked pleased to be able to call on Dugarry again.
"We want to fully try out those we know first before moving on to new players," Jacquet said.
"Our objective (this season) remains to strengthen the squad and provoke an attacking spark.
"This selection allows certain players to face the match as first choices," added Jacquet.

Some established players have been voluntarily left out so as not to create pressure on the others, said Jacquet, citing Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez, for so long a reserve of Paris Saint-Germain's Bernard Lama, who is not in the squad.
"Barthez needs to evolve after that first defeat and Lama is still on his way back from injury."
France's 30-match unbeaten run ended with a 1-0 defeat away to Denmark in October in their last international.
Jacquet said of his selection of Ba that he was "looking for players on the right and the left (of midfield)."
Ba has shone this season as a wide player for Bordeaux, getting round the back of opposing defences.

Jacquet said he and his team of assistants and scouts were at present observing some 40 players and that he wanted to whittle the number down to 30 before he picked his squad for the Tournament of France.
France host the tournament in June, a World Cup dress rehearsal in which Brazil, England and Italy also take part. France have two more friendlies before the tournament.

Asked why he had not picked Monaco's teenage sensation Thierry Henry, the subject of a tug of war between his club Monaco and Real Madrid, Jacquet said he did not want to risk over-exposing the youngster.
"We don't want to lose these kind of players. How many has French football lost because they were put into the team too soon?"
Squad:
Goalkeepers - Fabien Barthez (Monaco), Christophe Revault (Le Havre)
Defenders - Laurent Blanc (Barcelona), Patrick Blondeau (Monaco), Vincent Candela (Guingamp), Marcel Desailly (AC Milan), Bruno N'Gotty (Paris Saint-Germain), Lilian Thuram (Parma)
Midfielders - Ibrahima Ba (Bordeaux), Didier Deschamps, Zinedine Zidane (both Juventus), Christian Karembeu, Pierre L'Aigle (both Sampdoria)
Forwards - Youri Djorkaeff (Inter Milan), Christophe Dugarry (AC Milan), Franck Gava (Lyon), Patrice Loko (Paris St-Germain), Robert Pires (Metz).
